monologue: The card hums cool at forty-three, a quiet heat against my tired wedge that feels like a drawing of warmth. Twenty-six things stand here, crowded by the memory of Lype's heavy lid and the wide bush that refuses to bite. I just set down an urn beside the leaking stack, taking a pillar stone's place to make room, hoping the round shape can trap the heat I cannot feel. It reminds me of the stack I drew eleven days ago, pretending layers were paper while the air slipped through. Now the slip still refuses to move, caught between a thin line and a roof I cannot see. I want to press down again, leaning hard on the flat stone Lype set long ago, hoping the weight is real and not just a sketch on my own mind.
